key_insight: A PPO-based controller can coordinate battery, hydrogen, diesel, and grid exchange to keep a community microgrid highly renewable, reliable, and profitable under uncertainty.
engineering_relevance: This work shows how deep reinforcement learning can improve real-time energy management for hybrid microgrids with coupled storage assets and variable renewable supply.
method: Formulated the EMS as an 11-state Markov decision process with 3 continuous actions for battery, diesel, and hydrogen dispatch.
Used proximal policy optimization (PPO) to learn operational control for a grid-connected PV-wind-battery-electrolyzer-hydrogen-fuel-cell-diesel system.
Evaluated the policy on 8,760 hourly observations for a 1,000-household community in Rockhampton, Australia.
evidence_signal: Across a full year of hourly simulation, the learned policy achieved A$195,690.67 annual operating revenue, 91.2% renewable fraction, 99.77% load satisfaction, and 0.085 kg CO2/kWh carbon intensity under the stated boundary.
watch_item: Performance was sensitive to renewable variability and outage stress, and PPO training stability plus the chosen accounting boundary could affect reported outcomes.
paper_title: Deep Reinforcement Learning-Based Energy Management for Hydrogen-Enabled Community Microgrids Under Uncertainty
